scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: Original A1 independent assessment draft with ten new inference, argument or transfer questions. Content requires teacher approval.

tabs.title: Changes and Feelings
tabs.description: Notice how Mia feels and learns.

tabs.title: Try It Yourself
tabs.description: Choose a helpful action in a new situation.

questions.q: Why does Mia write a question mark in her book?
choices: She wants help with a part she does not understand.
She wants to give the book to Leo.
She wants to read only one page.
She wants to write a new story.
questions.explanation: The mark shows where the sentence about a train is difficult for her.

questions.q: How does the picture help Mia?
choices: It tells her how the story ends.
It gives her a clue about one new word.
It shows her which book to take home.
It helps her read the story faster.
questions.explanation: Leo points to the picture, and Mia understands one word by looking at it.

questions.q: Why does Mia still speak to her teacher?
choices: Leo is not her friend now.
She has lost her notebook.
There is another word she cannot understand.
She wants a different story.
questions.explanation: The teacher helps Mia with the second word after the picture helps with the first.

questions.q: How does Mia feel when she finds new words on Monday?
choices: Angry with her younger brother.
Happy that every word is easy.
Ready to teach the whole class.
Worried about the difficult reading.
questions.explanation: The first paragraph describes her concern when she cannot understand everything.

questions.q: Why does Mia smile after reading on Friday?
choices: Her teacher has given her a prize.
She can understand more than before.
She no longer needs to read books.
Leo has done the reading for her.
questions.explanation: The last paragraph says the new story remains difficult, but her understanding improves.

questions.q: What does Mia want to do after Friday?
choices: Stop reading until the next school year.
Read only with Leo's help.
Write a book about trains.
Keep practising her reading.
questions.explanation: Mia plans to practise again the next day because she can see progress.

questions.q: Sam does not understand a word in a picture story. What can he try?
choices: Look at the picture for a clue.
Stop reading the whole story.
Ask a friend to read every page.
Choose a word without looking.
questions.explanation: Mia uses a picture as a clue, so this is a suitable first step for Sam.

questions.q: A friend asks you to read a sentence again. What would Mia probably do?
choices: Hide the book in a bag.
Say that reading is not useful.
Try reading it one more time.
Ask the friend to do all the reading.
questions.explanation: Mia reads lines again for her brother and becomes more confident through practice.

questions.q: You have two new words to learn. Which plan is like Mia's?
choices: Forget the words and turn the page.
Write the words down and ask for help.
Read only the words you already know.
Wait until someone tells you the whole story.
questions.explanation: Mia asks about unfamiliar words and writes them in her notebook.

questions.q: What would be a good message to Mia after Friday?
choices: You must understand every word today.
You should never ask for help.
You only did well because reading was easy.
You kept trying and now understand more.
questions.explanation: Mia has made progress even though the reading is still challenging.
